terms.gloss: a dinner at a fixed price
terms.comment: A description of ours: no reference work searched (Traupman, Morgan–Owens, Levi–Bini) has a word for a set menu. Pretium certum is a fixed price; at midday say prandium certō pretiō. The courses are fercula, as when Suetonius says Augustus gave a dinner of three, cēnam ternīs ferculīs.

phrases.latin: Prandium certō pretiō sūmāmus: ternīs ferculīs cōnstat.
phrases.english: Let’s have the set lunch: it has three courses.

phrases.latin: Cēnam ternīs ferculīs aut cum abundantissimē sēnīs praebēbat, ut nōn nimiō sūmptū, ita summā cōmitāte.
phrases.english: He served a dinner of three courses, or of six at the most lavish, with no great expense but with the greatest good cheer.

sources: Lewis & Short: pretium · Lewis & Short: ferculum
